principles.name: Perceivable
principles.question: Can people perceive it?
principles.desc: Information and interface components must be presentable in ways people can perceive — whichever senses they rely on.

principles.name: Operable
principles.question: Can people operate it?
principles.desc: Components and navigation must work for everyone — by keyboard, touch, voice or switch — with enough time and without harm.

principles.name: Understandable
principles.question: Can people understand it?
principles.desc: Content and behavior must be readable, predictable, and forgiving of mistakes.

principles.name: Robust
principles.question: Will it work with assistive tech?
principles.desc: Content must be built so browsers and assistive technologies can interpret it reliably — today and as they evolve.

guidelines.name: Text Alternatives
guidelines.summary: Provide text alternatives for any non-text content.

guidelines.name: Time-based Media
guidelines.summary: Provide alternatives for audio and video.

guidelines.name: Adaptable
guidelines.summary: Create content that can be presented in different ways without losing structure.

guidelines.name: Distinguishable
guidelines.summary: Make it easier to see and hear content, including separating foreground from background.

guidelines.name: Keyboard Accessible
guidelines.summary: Make all functionality available from a keyboard.

guidelines.name: Enough Time
guidelines.summary: Give people enough time to read and use content.

guidelines.name: Seizures and Physical Reactions
guidelines.summary: Don’t design content in ways known to cause seizures or physical reactions.

guidelines.name: Navigable
guidelines.summary: Help people navigate, find content, and know where they are.

guidelines.name: Input Modalities
guidelines.summary: Make it easier to operate functionality through inputs beyond the keyboard.

guidelines.name: Predictable
guidelines.summary: Make pages appear and operate in predictable ways.

guidelines.name: Input Assistance
guidelines.summary: Help people avoid and correct mistakes.

guidelines.name: Compatible
guidelines.summary: Maximize compatibility with current and future tools, including assistive technologies.

criteria.title: Non-text Content
criteria.summary: Every meaningful image, icon and control has a text alternative. Decorative ones are hidden from assistive tech.

criteria.title: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.summary: Audio-only and video-only recordings come with a transcript or an equivalent alternative.

criteria.title: Captions (Prerecorded)
criteria.summary: Prerecorded video with sound has synchronized captions.

criteria.title: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.summary: Prerecorded video has audio description or a full text alternative.

criteria.title: Captions (Live)
criteria.summary: Live video with sound has captions.

criteria.title: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.summary: Prerecorded video describes important visual information in audio.

criteria.title: Sign Language (Prerecorded)
criteria.summary: Prerecorded video includes sign language interpretation.

criteria.title: Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.summary: Video pauses for longer descriptions when natural gaps are too short.

criteria.title: Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.summary: Prerecorded media has a full text alternative.

criteria.title: Audio-only (Live)
criteria.summary: Live audio-only content has a text alternative, such as live captions.

criteria.title: Info and Relationships
criteria.summary: Structure you show visually — headings, lists, tables, groups — also exists in code.

criteria.title: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.summary: When order affects meaning, the reading order in code matches it.

criteria.title: Sensory Characteristics
criteria.summary: Instructions don’t rely only on shape, size, position or sound — not just “tap the round button on the right”.

criteria.title: Orientation
criteria.summary: Content works in both portrait and landscape, unless one orientation is essential.

criteria.title: Identify Input Purpose
criteria.summary: Fields that collect personal details are identified, so browsers can autofill them.

criteria.title: Identify Purpose
criteria.summary: The purpose of components, icons and regions can be determined by software.

criteria.title: Use of Color
criteria.summary: Color is never the only way you show information, prompt an action, or mark an element.

criteria.title: Audio Control
criteria.summary: Audio that plays automatically for more than 3 seconds can be paused or muted.

criteria.title: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.summary: Text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 with its background — or 3:1 when it’s large.

criteria.title: Resize Text
criteria.summary: Text can be resized to 200% without losing content or function.

criteria.title: Images of Text
criteria.summary: Use real text rather than images of text, except for logos.

criteria.title: Contrast (Enhanced)
criteria.summary: Text has a contrast ratio of at least 7:1 — or 4.5:1 when it’s large.

criteria.title: Low or No Background Audio
criteria.summary: Speech recordings have little or no background sound.

criteria.title: Visual Presentation
criteria.summary: Text blocks can be adjusted: under 80 characters wide, not justified, generous line spacing.

criteria.title: Images of Text (No Exception)
criteria.summary: Images of text are used only for decoration, or where the presentation is essential.

criteria.title: Reflow
criteria.summary: Content reflows to a 320px-wide viewport without scrolling in two directions.

criteria.title: Non-text Contrast
criteria.summary: Icons, field borders, focus indicators and meaningful graphics have at least 3:1 contrast.

criteria.title: Text Spacing
criteria.summary: Nothing breaks when people increase line, paragraph, letter and word spacing.

criteria.title: Content on Hover or Focus
criteria.summary: Tooltips and popovers that appear on hover or focus can be dismissed, hovered over, and stay put.

criteria.title: Keyboard
criteria.summary: Everything can be operated with a keyboard alone.

criteria.title: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.summary: Keyboard focus never gets stuck inside a component.

criteria.title: Keyboard (No Exception)
criteria.summary: Everything can be operated with a keyboard — with no exceptions.

criteria.title: Character Key Shortcuts
criteria.summary: Single-key shortcuts can be turned off or remapped.

criteria.title: Timing Adjustable
criteria.summary: Time limits can be turned off, adjusted or extended.

criteria.title: Pause, Stop, Hide
criteria.summary: Moving, blinking or auto-updating content can be paused, stopped or hidden.

criteria.title: No Timing
criteria.summary: Timing isn’t an essential part of the activity.

criteria.title: Interruptions
criteria.summary: Interruptions such as alerts and updates can be postponed or turned off.

criteria.title: Re-authenticating
criteria.summary: When a session expires, people can sign back in and continue without losing data.

criteria.title: Timeouts
criteria.summary: People are told how long they can be inactive before data is lost.

criteria.title: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
criteria.summary: Nothing flashes more than three times in any one second.

criteria.title: Three Flashes
criteria.summary: Nothing flashes more than three times per second — no threshold exception.

criteria.title: Animation from Interactions
criteria.summary: Motion triggered by interaction can be turned off, unless it’s essential.

criteria.title: Bypass Blocks
criteria.summary: There’s a way to skip blocks that repeat on every page, like navigation.

criteria.title: Page Titled
criteria.summary: Every page or screen has a title that describes its topic or purpose.

criteria.title: Focus Order
criteria.summary: Focus moves through the page in an order that preserves meaning.

criteria.title: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.summary: The purpose of each link is clear from its text, together with its context.

criteria.title: Multiple Ways
criteria.summary: There’s more than one way to find a page — search, navigation, a sitemap.

criteria.title: Headings and Labels
criteria.summary: Headings and labels describe their topic or purpose.

criteria.title: Focus Visible
criteria.summary: Keyboard focus is always visible.

criteria.title: Location
criteria.summary: People can tell where they are — breadcrumbs, current-page states, step indicators.

criteria.title: Link Purpose (Link Only)
criteria.summary: The purpose of each link is clear from the link text alone.

criteria.title: Section Headings
criteria.summary: Content is organized with section headings.

criteria.title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.summary: A focused element is never completely hidden by sticky headers, banners or overlays.

criteria.title: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
criteria.summary: No part of a focused element is hidden by content you created.

criteria.title: Focus Appearance
criteria.summary: Focus indicators are big and bold: at least as large as a 2px outline, with 3:1 contrast against the unfocused state.

criteria.title: Pointer Gestures
criteria.summary: Multi-finger and path-based gestures have a single-pointer alternative.

criteria.title: Pointer Cancellation
criteria.summary: Actions fire on release, so people can slide off a target to cancel.

criteria.title: Label in Name
criteria.summary: A control’s accessible name contains the text of its visible label.

criteria.title: Motion Actuation
criteria.summary: Shake and tilt actions have an on-screen alternative and can be turned off.

criteria.title: Target Size (Enhanced)
criteria.summary: Pointer targets are at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels.

criteria.title: Concurrent Input Mechanisms
criteria.summary: People can switch between touch, mouse, keyboard and other inputs at any time.

criteria.title: Dragging Movements
criteria.summary: Anything done by dragging can also be done with single taps or clicks.

criteria.title: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.summary: Pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels — or spaced far enough from each other.

criteria.title: Language of Page
criteria.summary: The page’s main language is set in code, so screen readers pronounce it correctly.

criteria.title: Language of Parts
criteria.summary: Passages in a different language are marked up as such.

criteria.title: Unusual Words
criteria.summary: Jargon, idioms and unusual words have definitions available.

criteria.title: Abbreviations
criteria.summary: Abbreviations can be expanded or explained.

criteria.title: Reading Level
criteria.summary: Text above lower-secondary reading level comes with a simpler version or supplement.

criteria.title: Pronunciation
criteria.summary: Pronunciation is available where meaning depends on it.

criteria.title: On Focus
criteria.summary: Moving focus onto an element never triggers a surprise change of context.

criteria.title: On Input
criteria.summary: Changing a setting doesn’t unexpectedly change context, unless people are told first.

criteria.title: Consistent Navigation
criteria.summary: Navigation that repeats across pages stays in the same order.

criteria.title: Consistent Identification
criteria.summary: Components that do the same thing are labeled the same way.

criteria.title: Change on Request
criteria.summary: Changes of context only happen when people ask for them.

criteria.title: Consistent Help
criteria.summary: Help — contact details, chat, FAQs — appears in the same place on every page.

criteria.title: Error Identification
criteria.summary: Errors are identified, and described to the person in text.

criteria.title: Labels or Instructions
criteria.summary: Inputs have labels or instructions.

criteria.title: Error Suggestion
criteria.summary: When an error is detected and a fix is known, suggest it.

criteria.title: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
criteria.summary: Legal, financial and data submissions can be reversed, checked, or confirmed.

criteria.title: Help
criteria.summary: Context-sensitive help is available.

criteria.title: Error Prevention (All)
criteria.summary: Every submission can be reversed, checked, or confirmed.

criteria.title: Redundant Entry
criteria.summary: Don’t make people re-enter information they’ve already given in the same process.

criteria.title: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
criteria.summary: Logging in doesn’t require a memory test or puzzle — unless there’s an alternative such as paste, passkeys or a magic link.

criteria.title: Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)
criteria.summary: Logging in doesn’t require any cognitive test — not even recognizing objects or personal images.

criteria.title: Name, Role, Value
criteria.summary: Every component exposes its name, role and current state to assistive technologies.

criteria.title: Status Messages
criteria.summary: Status messages are announced to assistive tech without moving focus.
